Introduction and Definitions
1.1

Introduction:
These requirements regulate the restaurant sector to encourage investment and simplify
requirements for investors and beneficiaries by providing a suitable regulatory environment for
commercial investment, regulating the development process, and raising compliance with
municipal requirements, which will have a positive impact on the urban environment and urban
fabric of the city, food safety, and protecting public health, without prejudice to the approved
technical regulations and food standards.

1.2

Objectives:
These requirements have been issued to achieve the following objectives:
1.

Developing and improving the business environment in a manner that achieves the
aspirations and general objectives of both the individual and society.

2.

Simplifying procedures for those interested in investing in this field.

3.

Raising food safety standards.

1.3

Scope of Application:
These requirements apply to restaurants and cafes in both categories (with service – without
service), cloud kitchens, and food kiosks.

1.4

Terms and Definitions:

The Ministry:
Ministry of Municipalities and Housing.

Municipality / Sub-Municipality:
A legal entity with financial and administrative
independence that performs the functions
assigned to it under the relevant laws and
regulations.
Municipal License:
A written approval from the Municipality / SubMunicipality for a natural or legal person to
construct or open a premises for any activity
on a specific site in accordance with the
conditions specified in the law, the
Municipalities and Villages Law, and its related
regulations. This includes both commercial
and construction licenses.

Corridor:
A passageway connecting one space to
another.
Mezzanine Floor:
An intermediate floor between the floor
and ceiling of any space, not exceeding
one-third of the floor area. This area
may be increased to half the floor area
where an approved automatic fire
suppression and audible alarm system is
available.
Building Regulation:
Local municipal regulations that
determine how real estate properties are
developed within an urban area,
including land use type, coverage ratio,
permitted height, setbacks, and others.

Saudi Building Code:
A set of requirements and provisions, along
with related laws, implementing regulations,
and appendices pertaining to construction to
ensure public safety and health.

Sewage:
Wastewater discharged from the
establishment into the central sewage
system.

Urban Code:
A set of detailed controls and requirements for
regulating the urban form of buildings and
integrating them with their surroundings
through a defined identity, contributing to
enhancing the urban environment and
achieving optimal balance between people,
buildings, and the environment.

Well-Ventilated Intermediate Space:
An enclosed well-ventilated space, such
as a vestibule between restrooms and
food rooms. The purpose of ventilating
this enclosed space is to stabilize the
environment and prevent the transfer of
odors and contaminated air from the
restroom to the food room.

Urban Identity Design Guidelines:
Architectural requirements and guidelines
derived from heritage and natural elements,
covering design, materials, colors, and other
components used in urban works, applied
within a defined geographical area.

Food Establishment:
Any regulatory entity engaged in
activities related to food handling
throughout the food chain stages.

Site Area:
The total area of the land plot, enclosed within
its boundaries.

Setbacks:
The distances separating the building
boundaries from the site property boundaries.

Food Handler:
Any person who directly or indirectly
handles packaged or unpackaged food,
food equipment or utensils, or food
contact surfaces, and is therefore
required to comply with food safety
requirements.

Beneficiary:
A natural or legal person wishing to obtain
the services or products provided by the
establishment.

Container:
Used for collecting, transporting, or sorting
waste, typically made of metal or other
materials.

Approved Standard Specifications:
Standard specifications issued by the
Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality
Organization (SASO) and the Saudi Food
and Drug Authority (SFDA).

Bin:
A type of container used for collecting waste
inside the establishment, made of plastic,
metal, or other materials.

Technical Regulations:
Mandatory documents describing the
characteristics of food or its production
and manufacturing methods, and the
related regulatory instructions, including
terminology, symbols, packaging,
explanatory data, product labels, or
production methods.
SFDA:
Saudi Food and Drug Authority.

Compatible Activities:
Activities practiced at the same
establishment location that are of the
same nature as the licensed activity, do
not require additional area,and approved
in the Activity Card.
Additional Activities:
Activities practiced at the same establishment
location that are not of the same nature as the
licensed activity, require additional area, and are
approved in the Activity Card.
Activity Card:
Brief identification data of the ISIC (activity
number, activity name, detailed
description) along with the key spatial and
specific requirements for practicing the
activity, the name of the requirements
regulation
Unified Electronic Code (QR):
A digital service provided by the Saudi
Business Center in integration with
relevant government entities, allowing
consumers and inspectors to access
updated key data of economic
establishments via QR code.

Food-Grade Containers:
Containers made from material suitable for
direct food contact, with a smooth, non-porous
finish that is easy to clean. They must be
durable, leak-proof, and capable of being
tightly sealed or covered.
Allergens:
Components present in food that may cause an
allergic reaction.
Cross-Contact (with Allergens):
Cross-contact with allergens occurs when an
allergen unintentionally transfers to other foods
that are not supposed to contain that allergen.
Food:
Anything intended for human consumption,
whether raw, fresh, processed, or semiprocessed. Any substance used in the
manufacturing, preparation, or processing of
food is also considered food.
Food Hygiene:
The measures and conditions necessary for
controlling hazards and ensuring the suitability
of food for human consumption, considering its
intended use, including all measures required
to ensure food safety and wholesomeness.
Food Safety Management System:
An international standard developed to ensure
food safety and freedom from contaminants
throughout the food chain from farm to fork. It
is one of the international standards for Food
Safety Management Systems (FSMS). Food
establishments must comply with it by
monitoring, analyzing, and controlling critical
control points during food preparation and
processing to provide safe and wholesome
food.

Critical Control Points:
Specific points in the process where
failure to control hazards may result in
an unacceptable risk of foodborne
illness or injury.
High-Risk Foods:
Foods (such as meat, poultry, seafood,
dairy products, eggs, soups, and
cooked vegetables) that require
temperature control as they may
support rapid growth of pathogenic
bacteria. Control measures include
cooling or heating, requiring these
products to be kept at 60°C or above, or
5°C or below.
Product Shelf Life:
The period during which the product
retains its essential characteristics and
remains palatable, acceptable, and fit
for human consumption under specified
packaging, transport, and storage
conditions.

Uncooked Foods:
Food materials or ingredients that
require washing or cooking before they
become safe to eat, such as meat, fish,
game, poultry, and unwashed
vegetables.
Ready-to-Eat Foods:
Any food (including beverages) typically
consumed in its raw state, or any food
that has been handled, processed,
cooked, or prepared and can be
consumed without additional
processing, ready for consumption.
These meals may be chilled or frozen.
Food Unfit for Human Consumption:
Food that is unsuitable and
unacceptable for human consumption
according to its intended use, due to
spoilage, contamination with foreign
substances, or unintended changes in
its apparent or sensory characteristics.

Potable Water:
Water that meets legislative
requirements regarding its suitability for
drinking and use in food preparation,
being colorless, free from impurities,
odors, and disease-causing agents, and
compliant with regulations issued by
relevant authorities.
Pasteurization:
A form of heat treatment that kills most
but not all pathogens and spoilage
microorganisms present in milk and
other foods. During common
pasteurization, milk reaches 72°C for at
least 15 seconds.
Bain-Marie:
Equipment or device used in
restaurants, cafes, and hotels for
heating food and maintaining its
temperature within the containers inside
the bain-marie. The device consists of
stainless steel containers placed within
an electrically operated vessel. The
containers are heated through water
inside the vessel, and the temperature
is controlled via a thermostat.

Sous Vide:
A cooking technique that uses low
temperatures to slowly cook food in
sealed food-grade plastic bags.
Carpaccio:
A dish of meat or fish such as beef,
veal, venison, salmon, or tuna, cut into
thin slices and served raw as an
appetizer.

Cooking Time/Temperature:
A specific procedure necessary to
eliminate harmful microorganisms.
Internal Temperature:
The temperature at the center, which is
the thickest part of the food item.
Ambient Temperature:
The temperature of the surrounding
environment, typically used to mean
room temperature.

Relative Humidity:
The amount of water vapor in the air
expressed as a percentage of the amount
required for saturation at the same
temperature.
Danger Zone:
The temperature range between 5°C and
60°C where bacteria multiply rapidly. The
optimal temperature for bacterial growth
is typically approximately 37°C.

Communicable Disease:
Diseases that can be transmitted from
one person to another. The law requires
reporting certain diseases classified as
“notifiable diseases” to the local authority,
including food poisoning.
Toxins:
Any toxic substance often produced by
pathogens.

Hazards:
The probability and severity of an adverse
health effect resulting from exposure to
food hazards.

Microorganisms:
Any living organism, such as bacteria,
protozoa, or microscopic viruses. Those
that can cause harm to humans are often
referred to as pathogens.

Non-Conformity:
Failure to meet one of the requirements of
the administrative control system in place
for monitoring food safety.

Pests:
Any unwanted animals, insects, or birds
that enter and inhabit food premises or
food materials.

Recall:
Food recall is a mandatory action taken
by the manufacturer or distributor to
withdraw food from the sale, distribution,
or consumption stage to protect the public
from food safety risks or potential death.

Cleaning:
Removing food residues, visible dirt, food
particles, and waste from surfaces,
equipment, and fixtures using hot water,
detergents, and energy (such as
scrubbing).

First In, First Out (FIFO):
Managing inventory rotation following a
first in, first out approach.

Sanitizing:
Reducing microorganisms in the
environment to a level that does not
compromise food safety or suitability,
using chemical or physical methods.

Contamination:
The presence of a hazard source that
reaches or forms within food, including
undesirable substances, pathogenic or
spoilage microorganisms, or any other
materials that may affect food safety and
wholesomeness.
Cross-Contamination:
The transfer of contaminants to food due
to contact with contaminated food,
surfaces, or utensils.
Pathogens:
Any microorganism capable of causing
harm to humans.

Detergents:
Cleaning materials without sanitizing
properties, used for general cleaning such
as removing grease and food residues.
Sanitizer:
A chemical substance for sanitizing
equipment, work surfaces, hands,
vegetables, and salad ingredients. Some
sanitizers contain detergents that aid in
cleaning.
Clean-in-Place (CIP):
A cleaning method used for equipment
that cannot be disassembled for routine
cleaning.

Heat Sanitizing:
Can be performed using very hot water,
hot air, or steam, at a temperature of
82°C or above.
Sterilization:
Heat or chemical treatment to eliminate
all microorganisms and viruses.

1.5

Restaurant Activity Classification:
1. Restaurants with Service:
Food establishments where meals are prepared and served for consumption in the
attached dining hall specifically designed for this purpose, or for takeaway.

2. Restaurants without Service:
Food establishments where meals are prepared and produced without providing dine-in
service.

3. Cafes:
Establishments that primarily focus on preparing and serving specialty coffee or other
coffee-based beverages, in addition to tea and seasonal drinks. Cafes may also serve
food or light snacks that are typically pre-prepared or sourced externally and not prepared
on-site. The cafe may provide dine-in service or takeaway orders.

4. Cloud Kitchens:
A restaurant dedicated entirely to preparing food for delivery. Multiple restaurants often share the
same kitchen, known as a cloud kitchen complex. A cloud kitchen does not require a dedicated
location for receiving customers. All meals and prices are displayed through a digital platform,
and orders and payments are processed electronically.

5. Food Kiosks:
Small standalone commercial activities that may be without walls, with a special design in
line with the city's urban identity, where food products are prepared, sold, and served at
locations designated by the Municipality / Sub-Municipality.

Technical Requirements
4.1

General Technical Requirements:
1. All design and supervision work must be carried out by engineering offices certified by the
Ministry.
2. Fixtures, installations, and equipment must be designed, constructed, positioned, and
installed where applicable in a manner that does not pose a food safety risk through
contamination, allows effective cleaning of surrounding floors, walls, and ceilings, and
does not obstruct corridors.
3. When connecting certain fixtures, installations, and equipment to a water source or
drainage or cleaning equipment and services, an appropriate connection to sewage lines
must be provided.
4. Adding a drive-through service is permitted, provided it is included in the building permit.

4.2

Architectural Requirements:
1. The Saudi Building Code requirements must be complied with (including but not limited to:

structural, electrical, mechanical, ventilation and air conditioning, plumbing, energy
efficiency requirements, and others) regarding restaurant activities. All work, installations,
and materials must be carried out in accordance with the approved standard specifications.
2. The establishment must be designed to accommodate the areas and spaces designated for

food handling, cooking, storage, equipment layout planning, and the dining hall, among
other considerations.

3. The food preparation and production area must be away from any contamination.

Example:

Example:

4. Ensuring that food preparation and storage facilities are adequate for safe food production,

suitable for the expected volume of operations.
5. Ensuring food safety from the arrival of food through to serving, through effective means for

controlling potential contamination.
6. Ensuring effective cleaning access to all interior parts of the structure that require cleaning.
7. All buildings must be protected against pest access and harborage.
8. The sewage system must be designed and installed so as not to contaminate the potable

water supply, food production areas, or food contact surfaces and equipment.
9. Overhead utility pipes must not pose a contamination risk from foreign objects through paint

flaking or rust, and must be manufactured and covered with suitable insulating material to
minimize dirt accumulation.

4.2.1 Interior and Exterior Structural Requirements
1. The design and construction of restaurants must meet the following requirements:
• Designating an approved food preparation area where only food handling activities take

place, clearly visible to service recipients or separated by transparent glass, without being
covered or concealed, with the option of using cameras and screens.
2. It is recommended that the establishment layout promotes safe food handling, includes

designated areas or time-divided zones for uncooked food handling, and is designed so
that food operations flow in one direction only, from receiving to storage, preparation,
cooking, through to packaging, serving, or distribution, according to the following criteria:
• Following a sequential workflow model from food entry to the kitchen, through storage and

preparation, to serving ready-to-eat food, to minimize contamination.
• Designating separate areas for uncooked and ready-to-eat foods, and designing buildings

to enable collection and storage of orders or waste without passing through food
preparation rooms.

4.2.2 Ground Oven (Tannour) Requirements
1. It must be equipped with an oven with firebrick walls, with a conical funnel connected to a

chimney for smoke discharge, with an air extraction fan at its end, or equipped with electric
or gas burners, to prevent smoke contamination and protect the environment.
2. Each oven must have two stainless steel metal covers matching the oven opening size.

3. Providing a channel with a width of (30) cm and a depth of (60) cm adjacent to the oven, for

placing sand and red soil.
4. Using two layers of thick cloth or equivalent, such as: (tent fabric), placed on top to prevent

cooking heat from escaping, with the cloth to be washed regularly to maintain cleanliness.

4.3

Facade and General Appearance Requirements
1.

The shop/establishment facade design must follow the Urban Code or the Urban Identity
Design Guidelines for the area where the activity is located. If unavailable, the facade
design shall follow what was approved in the license issued by the Municipality / SubMunicipality.

2.

Installing electrical wiring, plumbing pipes, and other service extensions and external air
conditioning units on the building facade or visibly on the roof is prohibited.

3.

If glass is used in facades, it must be tempered (Securit) glass or equivalent, with a
thickness of no less than 12 mm.

Example:

4.4

Staircase and Exterior Sidewalk Requirements:
1.

Accessibility requirements for persons with disabilities must be met in accordance with
Chapter (1009) and Section (11) of the Saudi Building Code( SBC-201) and the Simplified
Guide to Universal Accessibility Standards for Establishments.

2.

Exterior staircases of the building must be made of safe, slip-resistant, and highly durable
materials, including granite, treated marble, rough epoxy resin coating, ceramic, porcelain,
and similar materials.

3.

A ramp for persons with disabilities must be provided within the shop/establishment
boundaries. Shops located in buildings that provide accessibility requirements are exempt.

4.

The ramp must be free from defects and must not affect the exterior sidewalk or cause any
visual distortion.

5.

The shop/establishment entrance staircase or ramp must be placed within the
establishment boundaries.

6.

Staircases, exterior sidewalks, and ramps for persons with disabilities must be free from
any installations or equipment that obstruct entry to or exit from the shop/establishment, or
rapid evacuation in case of accidents, emergencies, or injuries.

7.

The permitted slopes must be followed according to the Universal Accessibility Standards
for Establishments for the sidewalk ramp for persons with disabilities
Example:

4.5

Wall, Ceiling, Flooring, Lighting, Window, and Door
Requirements:
1. The surfaces of walls and partition walls must be moisture-resistant, fire-resistant, and easy

to clean.
2. Walls must be light-colored for easy visibility of accumulated food residues (in food

preparation, production, and storage areas). Ledges, protrusions, and recesses in the
design must be avoided. Walls must be clad with durable and easy-to-clean materials, with
a minimum height of 1.80 m from floor level. The following are examples of suitable wall
surfaces:
• Ceramic panels.
• Interior or exterior plaster coated with washable paint.
• Waterproof cement fill.

• Epoxy resin and similar coatings.
• Stainless steel sheets.

3. Door and window design must meet the following:

• Solid, tight-fitting, self-closing doors.
• Wire mesh, air curtains, or plastic strip curtains or similar, properly designed and installed

on doors and windows that open to the outside.
• Doors within preparation areas must be self-closing with sanitizable fittings, free from

decorative corners and protrusions where dirt accumulates.
• Using wood without a protective coating is prohibited. Suitable door materials include:

metal (typically stainless steel), wood coated with a protective waterproof layer such as
paint, gloss, or varnish, plastic, or non-porous panels.
4. Floors must be finished with materials appropriate for the type of activity, consistent with

the Saudi General Building Code (SBC-201).
5. Floors must be light-colored in food preparation areas to distinguish the area and clearly

see food residues.
6. Floors in exposed areas and exterior sidewalks must be sloped toward drainage at no more

than 2% for rainwater and wash water drainage.
7. The angles between walls and floors must not be sharp, with rounded or 45-degree angled

junctions to facilitate cleaning and sanitizing and prevent contaminant accumulation.
Example:

8. Suspended and exposed ceilings in food handling, storage, and preparation areas must be:
• In good condition, easy to clean, smooth to prevent flaking, and non-porous.
• Allowing pest inspection in the space above the ceiling (between the original and

suspended ceiling).
• Made from non-flammable materials.
8. Fixed lighting fixtures must be adequately designed for food preparation, ensuring ease of

cleaning and preventing dirt accumulation.

4.6

Balcony (Mezzanine) Requirements:
1. Staircases and the balcony (mezzanine) must be constructed in accordance with Saudi

Building Code requirements and Civil Defense requirements.
2. The balcony (mezzanine) constructed in food handling, storage, and preparation areas

must be away from food handling areas to prevent any residues, splashed liquids, or drops
from contaminating food.
3. Staircases in food handling, storage, and preparation areas must have closed risers made

from easy-to-clean and non-porous materials.

4.7

Ventilation Requirements:
1.

The ventilation system design must comply with the Saudi Building Code.

2.

Ventilation openings must be covered from the outside with a metal mesh to prevent insect
and rodent entry.

3.

The ambient temperature must not exceed 25°C while ensuring no condensation of vapors
or dust.

4.

The Chimney Guide for Commercial Activities issued by the Ministry must be followed.

Example:

4.8

Attached Storage Requirements:

1. A storage facility for storing activity-related materials is permitted, provided its area does

not exceed 25% of the total area stated in the license or 150 m², whichever is less.

4.9

Fire Prevention and Protection Requirements:
1. All requirements in the Saudi Building Code for Fire Protection (SBC-801) must be followed.

Example:

4.10

Restroom Requirements:
4.10.1 Restroom Requirements

1. It is recommended to provide a minimum of one restroom serving customers.
2. Restrooms located inside the food establishment must meet the following:
• They must be away from any food handling areas. If this is not possible, restrooms and

food handling areas must be separated by well-ventilated intermediate spaces.
• They must not open directly onto a room where food is handled.
• They must be equipped with handwashing sinks, with soap and paper towels or a hand

dryer near the restrooms.
• They must be equipped with foot-operated waste bins to prevent hand contamination when

opening them.
• They must not be used for storing items such as aprons or food materials.

Basic Installation Requirements:
5.4.1 Food Contact Surface Requirements

1.

Food contact surfaces must be made from suitable, safe, non-corrosive materials that are
smooth and non-porous (do not absorb any liquids, fats, or food), and are easily and
effectively cleaned and sanitized.
Example:

5.4.2 Water and Ice Usage Requirements
1.

Water used inside the food establishment must be potable, available at the appropriate
pressure and temperature for the following purposes:
• Cleaning food and its equipment.
• Conducting all food production processes (such as water bath, sous vide, or bain-marie),

or using it in food recipes or food preparation.
Example:

• Preparing ice or steam or using it in beverage blending machines.
• Cleaning food contact surfaces or the hands of food handlers.

2.

All equipment and tools used in ice production, distribution, and storage must be kept
away from contamination sources, and cleaned and sanitized internally on a regular basis.
Such equipment must be hygienically designed to prevent drainage water backflow.

3.

Ice machines must have suitable covers to prevent dust or dirt from entering pipes, sloped
drains, and openings, and to protect against droplets from weather elements (such as wind
or rain), pests, and other environmental contaminants.

4.

Ice scoops must not be in contact with ice pieces during storage.

5.4.3 Equipment and Utensil Washing Facility Requirements
1. An area for cleaning, sanitizing, and drying all food contact equipment such as utensils,

pots, and serving dishes must be provided, separate from food preparation and production
areas.
2.

Washing food items or workers' hands in sinks designated for washing equipment and
utensils is prohibited.

3.

For machine washing, dishwashers must be supplied with detergent and sanitizer.
Dishwashers must rely on either hot water for glassware or chemical sanitizer for
sanitizing.

4.

Manual or machine dishwashing is permitted based on the establishment's needs.

5.

Effective cleaning and sanitizing tools must be provided.

6.

Equipment washing sinks must be supplied with hot and cold water (suitable for human
use).

5.4.4 Handwashing Sink Requirements
1. At least one handwashing sink must be available within the food preparation area, ensuring

the preparation area is not contaminated and that these sinks are clean, in good condition,
and provide hot water.
2. They must contain liquid or foam soap dispensers, disposable paper towel dispensers or a

hand dryer, and be equipped with a waste container.
3. A sign must be placed above it indicating it is designated for handwashing only and must

not be used for any other purpose.
5.4.5 Equipment and Utensil Requirements
1. Equipment and utensils must be made from food-safe materials and comply with the

approved standard specifications.
2. Stoves and ovens operating on gas, electricity, charcoal, or other safe materials for food

preparation must be provided based on the establishment's needs.
3. Separate equipment for uncooked and ready-to-eat foods must be provided, including

separate items of the following: refrigerators, freezers, display units, work areas,
equipment, utensils, and kitchen sinks.
4. Using wooden cutting boards or knives with wooden handles for cutting meat, poultry, fish,

and other items is prohibited. They must be replaced with boards and knives with handles
made from food-safe materials such as plastics for easy cleaning.
5. Equipment and utensils used in food preparation and handling (including single-use items)

must be stored in a designated food-safe location.

5.5

Food Safety Requirements:
Food safety requirements in accordance with the laws, regulations, and
specifications issued by the Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA)
5.5.1 Food Receiving Provisions
1. The food establishment must inspect all deliveries to ensure they are stored within the

required temperature range, especially chilled or frozen deliveries, properly packaged, with
valid expiry dates, and free from any signs of pest infestation, in compliance with Section
5.5.2 of these requirements.
2. During internal transport of chilled and frozen food, it must be transferred immediately to

temperature-controlled storage areas appropriate for the product's storage requirements, to
minimize time outside the temperature control range. Good practice is that chilled food
should not remain outside the refrigerator for more than 20 minutes during transfer.
3. During food transport, the food establishment must comply with the technical regulation

(SFDA.FD/GSO 323) Requirements for (SFDA.FD/GSO 2504).
4. When receiving frozen food, its temperature must not be above -18°C. If temperatures are

outside the specified range, deliveries must be rejected.
5. When receiving chilled food, its temperature must not exceed 4°C. The food establishment

must verify food deliveries to ensure they have not exceeded the specified temperature
range and reject any non-compliant food.
6. Temperature checks for high-risk foods must be conducted upon arrival using a non-contact

thermometer or a clean, sanitized temperature probe, and results must be recorded and
documented.

5.5.2 Purchased Materials, Products, and Services Control Requirements
1. All food products, tools, and equipment used in food establishments must comply with

Saudi standard specifications.
2. Fresh meat delivered to the food establishment must be slaughtered at a licensed

slaughterhouse and stamped with the slaughterhouse's approved seal.
3. When serving food raw or lightly cooked (such as raw shellfish, sushi, tartare, steak and

carpaccio), the food establishment must obtain information from the supplier about the
source of these foods when applicable, and these records must be retained.

4. When purchasing packaging materials and single-use materials, the food establishment

must ensure they are food-grade. When purchasing personal protective equipment (such
as: head covers, gloves), they must be suitable for use in food preparation.

5.5.3 Storage Provisions
1. Food establishments must have adequate storage for all items needed for operation,

including food, food ingredients, equipment, non-food materials such as utensils, linens,
single-use items, packaging, and chemicals.
2. Storing food, its ingredients, equipment, and packaging materials in the following locations

is prohibited:
•

Employee changing rooms, their lockers, restrooms, or mechanical rooms.

• Chemical or pesticide storage areas.
• Dirty or contaminated equipment storage areas.

3. All storage areas must be clean and dry to minimize contamination risks from foreign

objects and prevent pest harborage. They must contain adequate shelving for all materials,
with sufficient spacing for visual inspection and effective cleaning. Shelving must be made
from durable, corrosion-resistant, and non-porous materials.
4. Storage must be at a height of 15 cm above the floor, 5 cm from the wall, and 30 cm from

the ceiling where possible. For frozen storage, sufficient space between items must be
provided to allow effective air circulation.
5. Non-food materials such as charcoal, detergents, sanitizers, pesticides, and similar

products must be stored in designated areas, away from food handling areas to avoid
potential contamination.
Example:

6. The food establishment must comply with Technical Regulation No. ( 150-1 SFDA.FD)

Food Product Shelf Life – Part One: Mandatory Shelf Life Periods.
Food must be stored to ensure protection from water leakage, pest infestation, or any other
contamination risk.

7.

8. When opening a sewage drain, all exposed food must be removed from the food room

where the drain is located.
9. All food must be covered when stored and kept in food-safe containers to prevent

contamination if original packaging is unavailable. Labels must be placed showing the
product name, opening or thawing date, and “use before” date (once opened) to allow
effective stock rotation.
10. Food storage areas must be capable of maintaining food at appropriate temperatures:

• Chilled food at 0°C to 4°C.
• Frozen food at below -18°C.
• Food stored at ambient temperature between 15°C and 25°C.
11. Humidity must be between 60–65% in ambient temperature food storage areas.
12. Food must be stored according to the requirements in the product specifications where

available.
13. The food establishment must monitor packaging integrity and raw material temperatures.
14.

Storing uncooked food above ready-to-eat food is prohibited.

15. Ready-to-eat food must be stored above uncooked meat, poultry, fish, and eggs, as well

as above unprocessed and uncooked vegetables.
16. Partially consumed containers must be properly sealed to prevent contamination. If

containers are made of galvanized tin, the remaining contents must be transferred to safe,
hygienic, airtight plastic containers.
17. When a food establishment provides an allergen statement in its menu, clear labels must

be placed on food containing allergens, and allergen-containing food must be stored
separately from allergen-free counterparts.
18. Direct storage on the floor is prohibited.
19. Stock rotation must be a routine procedure to ensure food is consumed before its expiry

date.
20. Ingredients must be used and consumed within the shelf life specified by the manufacturer,

and manufacturer's storage guidelines must be followed.

21. Food ingredients must be disposed of if they show any signs of spoilage such as changes

in color, taste, odor, or texture.
22. In case of power outage, the following must be observed:
• Do not open refrigerator or freezer doors during the power outage.
• Dispose of all chilled food exposed to temperatures exceeding 4°C for more than two

hours. If any signs of thawing appear on frozen food, it must be used immediately or
disposed of.

5.5.4 Preparation Provisions
1. The laws, instructions, implementing regulations, and technical regulations issued by the

Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) must be complied with when preparing any type of
food.
2. Food must be inspected before use to ensure it is in good condition, with no mold, foul

odors, decomposition, or any other signs of spoilage.
3.

Ready-to-eat food handling requirements (SFDA.FD/GSO 1909) must be referred to.

4. Foods consumed uncooked, such as beef carpaccio, must be kept refrigerated until ordered

and served immediately.

Example:

5. When the food establishment prepares fresh fruits and vegetables, the following must be

observed:
• Inspecting fresh fruits and vegetables and disposing of damaged ones.
• Providing a dedicated sink for preparing and washing fruits and vegetables.
• Peeling, trimming, or removing outer parts entirely as needed.
• Washing them thoroughly in water suitable for human use.
• Sanitizing leafy vegetables consumed directly without cooking using safe sanitizers

according to standard specifications.
6. When handling uncooked meat, poultry, or fish, they must not be washed to avoid

spreading contamination. They must be prepared using designated cutting boards and tools
that are thoroughly cleaned after use. All areas must be cleaned and sanitized immediately
after preparing uncooked food.

7. Bags must be protected from punctures caused by bones or sharp objects during vacuum

packaging and storage.
8. Hot food must be cooled in a blast chiller before vacuum packaging.
9. Vacuum packaging food more than once is prohibited.
10. Only approved food-grade bags suitable for food contact must be used for vacuum

packaging.
11. When the food establishment prepares shawarma, the General Requirements for

Shawarma Preparation and Handling (GSO 1060:2022) must be followed.
12. Regarding dry-aged meat preparation, the food establishment may purchase dry-aged meat

from a licensed supplier or age the meat itself.
13. If the establishment performs the aging process itself, it must have the necessary

equipment, including aging cabinets, coolers, and temperature and humidity control tools.
14. Dry aging must only be performed in a chamber where temperature, air speed, and

humidity can be controlled, and only dry-aged meat may be stored in it.
15. All areas containing dry aging cabinets and coolers must meet the following:
• Temperature between 0.5°C and +3°C.
• Relative humidity between 75% and 85%.
• Air speed between 0.2 m/s and 0.5 m/s.
• These parameters must be monitored at least daily.
16. Salt blocks must not be used alone.
17. When preparing dry-aged meat for serving, it must be prepared separately from other

meats and ingredients to prevent microbial contamination.

5.5.5 Sauce Preparation Controls
1. The blend's data and ingredients must be documented and their source known to the food

establishment.
2. Must be kept refrigerated at a maximum temperature of 4°C, away from direct sunlight and

contamination sources.
3. The sauce container must be tightly sealed, with production and expiry dates clearly

indicated according to requirements and specifications.
4. Must have natural sensory characteristics, free from undesirable odor and taste or foreign

materials such as insects and rancidity.
5. Using fresh eggs and ready-made sauces in preparing sauces is prohibited. Pasteurized

egg products may be used.
6. The acidity (pH level) in sauces must not exceed 4.
7. After confirming the pH level of the sauce is compliant, adding any other materials to it is

prohibited.
8. Raw materials used in sauce manufacturing must be heat-treated or dried before use.
9. Preparing mayonnaise inside the establishment is prohibited. Only mayonnaise produced in

licensed factories may be used.

5.5.6 Cooking Provisions
1.

Correct cooking procedures must be followed to avoid the danger zone. The internal
temperature of food must not be less than 75°C when cooking raw food.
• All temperatures mentioned refer to food temperature, not air temperature. Therefore, any

recorded temperature readings must represent the food temperature, not the air
temperature in all parts of the food holding unit.
• A temperature probe must be used to verify food temperature and not rely solely on

temperature readings displayed by built-in equipment thermometers.
• Lower cooking temperatures are acceptable provided the internal temperature is

maintained for a specified period as follows:
o

60°C for no less than 45 minutes.

o

65°C for no less than 10 minutes.

o

(70) °C for no less than 2 minutes..

o

75°C for 30 seconds.

o

80°C for 6 seconds.

2. Liver must be cooked thoroughly to kill bacteria.

3. For certain meats such as beef, lamb, and rare fish, cooking temperatures below 75°C are

acceptable provided the outer surface is sufficiently cooked to kill bacteria.
4. No part of the meat may remain pink in cooked poultry.
5. During cooking of raw food, it must not come into contact with or drip onto cooked food.
6. During meat cooking, the surface must be seared with heat to kill any harmful bacteria, and

the meat must be turned frequently during cooking.
7. Whole cuts of rare meat (beef and lamb) may be served provided the surface has been

sufficiently heat-treated.
8. Serving burgers rare is prohibited because the meat is cut and minced before preparation,

meaning not all meat surfaces can be seared to kill harmful bacteria.
9. Liquid dishes such as soups and sauces must be cooked in wide pans rather than deep

pans to ensure the heat source covers the entire base of the pan so liquids cook slowly.
10. Microwaves do not cook or reheat food evenly. Therefore, food prepared in microwaves

must be stirred or rotated to distribute heat evenly, then left covered for at least two minutes
after cooking to achieve even heat distribution.
11. When preparing ice cream, it must be pasteurized to 85°C before being subjected to blast

chilling and freezing.
12. When frying, the Health Requirements Guide for Frying Fats and Oils must be referred to.
13. All additives such as spices, herbs, flavorings, taste enhancers, and colorings must be

permitted and added in quantities not exceeding the permitted amounts according to the
approved standard specifications for each type. The technical regulation on Permitted Food
Additives (SFDA.FD/GSO 2500), which specifies the permitted additives and their allowed
concentrations, must be complied with.
14. If the food establishment needs to change or substitute an ingredient that would result in a

change in allergen status, all allergen information provided to workers and customers must
be updated to reflect this change.

15. When using air or gas as an ingredient or in direct contact with a product or package, it

must be of food-grade purity (with a certificate of conformity), filtered or clean, and free from
microbial contamination.
16. When workers taste food, only clean and sanitized utensils must be used. Utensils must be

cleaned and sanitized immediately after tasting and before tasting any other food or the
same food again. Tasting the same product twice with the same utensils is prohibited.
Single-use utensils are preferred.

5.5.7 Hot Food Cooling Requirements
1. Cooked food to be refrigerated must be cooled until the thermal center temperature drops

below 10°C within two hours. The product must then be stored immediately at 4°C and
used within two to three days of preparation.
2. When preparing high-risk foods at room temperature then storing at chilled temperature

before serving, they must be cooled from room temperature to 4°C maximum within two
hours, including foods containing canned or reconstituted ingredients.
3. Products intended for ambient temperature consumption such as baked goods or desserts

may be cooled on open trays or shelves before ambient display.
4. When a product is cooked, cooled, stored, and used within its permitted shelf life, within two

to three days for example, it may then be used as an ingredient in another dish prepared for
immediate consumption.
5. Food cooling methods include:
• Using the blast chiller, following the manufacturer's instructions.
• Ensuring containers are cold before use.
• Using an ice water bath, ensuring food is in tightly covered containers.
• Cutting large meat portions into pieces or slices before cooling.
• Dividing food into portions and placing them in smaller containers.
• Placing food in the appropriate refrigerator or freezer, ensuring it is protected from

contamination and does not cause a significant rise in the temperature of other food
already in the refrigerator or freezer.

5.5.8 Reheating Requirements
1. When reheating food, equipment capable of effectively heating to an internal temperature of

(75) °C must be used to ensure food safety.
2.

Reheated food must be consumed immediately or placed in hot food holding equipment.

3. Re-cooling any food that has been reheated is prohibited.

Example:

5.5.9 Food Freezing Requirements
1.

Chilled food or food left to cool after cooking must be frozen as quickly as possible.

2. Food establishments must ensure freezers operate correctly and maintain a temperature of

at least -18°C through checks performed at opening and closing according to internal
procedures. Manufacturers may specify higher temperatures for certain products (such as
ice cream).

5.5.10 Food Thawing Requirements
1. Food must be completely thawed before cooking or consumption unless intended for

cooking from frozen. Food must only be thawed once, and manufacturer's instructions for
food products must be followed.
2. When thawing in the refrigerator, food must be placed in a container to catch any liquids or

placed at the bottom of the refrigerator to prevent cross-contamination from dripping onto
other food.
3. When thawing food, one of the following methods may be used:
• Thawing food in the refrigerator.
• Using the "defrost" setting on the microwave.
• Placing food in a covered container under running cold or ice water.
4. Packaged frozen food may be thawed at ambient temperature if the manufacturer's

instructions allow, such as baked goods, fruits, or grated nuts.

5.5.11 Display Provisions
1. When displaying food, the food establishment must take all practical measures to protect it
from contamination.
2. The food establishment must not display any ready-to-eat food not intended for selfservice for sale on any table without a responsible person present, unless the food is
sealed, packaged in containers, or wrapped in a manner that protects it from potential
contamination.
3. When displaying food, temperature controls for chilled and frozen food must be followed,
and all products must remain within the appropriate temperature range so they do not thaw
or become unsafe to eat.
4. Chilled food must be consumed within two hours of removal from the refrigerator or
disposed of.

5. Hot food must be kept at a temperature above 60°C. If displayed outside the hot food
holding unit, it must be consumed within two hours or disposed of.
6. Frozen food such as ice cream must be displayed in a frozen display unit.
7. If uncooked food and ready-to-eat food are kept in shared display units, they must be
separated using physical barriers.

8. When using baskets for food display, food must be placed on clean single-use liners.
9. Food may be displayed in wooden display units only if they are treated to be cleanable and
food-safe.

Fresh Fish Display
1. When displaying fresh fish, it must be kept at ice-melting temperature with the catch date
displayed. When placing fish in or on a layer of crushed ice, good contact between the ice
and fish must be maintained throughout the display period.
2. All ice used for displaying fish must be made from potable water.

Ready-to-Eat Food Display
1. Ready-to-eat food must be served in containers with tight-fitting lids. If this is not possible
and the food is left unpackaged, the following supervisory controls must be applied:
•

A responsible food handling employee must supervise the display area to ensure
immediate removal of any food contaminated by a customer or potentially exposed to
contamination from the display unit.

•

Serving utensils for each type of food must be separated, or other distribution methods
must be provided to minimize the potential for food contamination.

•

Protective barriers such as "sneeze guards" must be installed to minimize the potential for
customer-caused contamination.

5.5.12 Hot Food Holding Requirements
1. The following procedures must be applied to maintain temperatures and keep food hot. If

the establishment does not have hot food holding equipment, food must be prepared for
immediate consumption.
• Appropriate equipment must be used to keep food hot during serving, following the

equipment manufacturer's instructions.
Example:

• Equipment must be regularly inspected to ensure effective operation.
• Equipment must reach the required temperature before placing any food inside.
• Hot food must be held at no less than 60°C and consumed within 6 hours. If the

temperature drops below 60°C, food must be consumed within 4 hours or disposed of.
• If food is removed from hot holding equipment for display, it must not be mixed with food

already on display.

5.5.13 Temperature Control Provisions
1. The food establishment must implement a temperature monitoring system, which can be

achieved through the following methods:
• Installing a device with a digital display or inserting a thermometer into equipment to

display the temperature. If no digital display or alternative is available, the product
temperature itself must be checked.
• Using a device labeled "for temperature checking only" placed in the equipment for manual

temperature checking.

5.5.14 Serving Provisions

1. It is recommended that the dining hall be located at the front of the establishment where
possible. It may be divided into rooms, open plan, or use fixed or movable short partitions,
and furnished with appropriate furniture.

2. All food must be served in clean plates and beverages in clean glasses or cups, or in
single-use food-grade portable containers or packages.
3. Using any cracked, chipped, or damaged tableware is prohibited.
4. Using the dining hall for storage is prohibited.
5. Reusing food that has been previously served or sold is prohibited.

5.5.15 Product Information Disclosure Requirements
1. The SFDA requirements for products with health and nutrition claims must be followed.
2. The claims regulation must be complied with when labeling food products, according to:
•

(SFDA.FD 2333) Requirements for Foods with Health and Nutritional Claims.

• (SFDA.FD 5016) Requirements for nutritionally balanced meals in menus of food

establishments serving food to consumers outside the home.
3. The time and expiry date must be placed on chilled and ready-to-eat foods prepared and

stored in food service establishments. For example: consume within one hour of purchase;
store at below 4°C or -18°C.
4. Pre-packaged food must comply with all applicable labeling requirements as stipulated in

the GCC Technical Regulation (SFDA.FD GSO9) "Pre-Packaged Food Labels", including:
• Food item name.
• List of ingredients.
• Allergen details, if applicable:

(Celery, gluten, crustaceans, eggs, fish, lupin, milk, mollusks, mustard, tree nuts, peanuts,
sesame seeds, sulfur dioxide, soy).
5. If commercially manufactured pre-packaged food is sold in individual packages, it must

bear, or have stamped or printed on its label or elsewhere, a date mark showing production
and expiry dates as specified and approved by food regulatory authorities.
6.

The date mark on the original package must not be removed, erased, altered, obscured,
placed over another date, or tampered with in any way.

7. Usage instructions after opening the original package must be provided when applicable,

for example: "Keep refrigerated after opening and consume within three days."
8. Compliance with these instructions is not required for baked goods typically consumed

within 24 hours, where the production date alone is acceptable.
9. Labels and accompanying explanatory data must be in Arabic. When another language is

used, it must be alongside the Arabic language.

10. The food establishment must comply with the regulatory requirements related to customer

allergen information as stipulated in:
• SFDA Regulation, Specification No. (SFDA.FD GSO 2605) regarding allergen disclosure

in menus of food establishments serving food to consumers outside the home, and the
GCC Technical Regulation GSO 9 regarding pre-packaged food labels, as applicable.
• Specification No. (SFDA.FD 5028) regarding food allergen disclosure in pre-packaged

food labels.
• Specification No. (SFDA.GSO 1909) regarding ready-to-eat food handling requirements.
11. Food establishments must provide information about the fourteen specified allergens and

their protein derivatives. If any of these food allergens are present at any level, whether as
an ingredient, within a mixture, as a food additive, or as a processing aid:
• Pre-packaged food must comply with allergen information requirements stipulated in the

GCC Technical Regulation (SFDA.FD GSO 9) regarding pre-packaged food labels.
• For food prepared for immediate consumption exempt from labeling requirements, allergen

information must be displayed through one or more of the following means (menu,
package, display board, product ticket) or by directing the customer to obtain such
information from a trained staff member.

5.5.16 Non-Conformity Handling Requirements
1. If the food establishment determines that a food item or ingredient may be unsafe or unfit for

consumption, it must take the following actions:
• Taking immediate action to control defective ingredients and dishes prepared from them.
• Separating any remaining defective product, labeling it "unfit for human consumption," and

storing it securely.
• Carefully disposing of all defective products, ensuring they do not enter the human or

animal food chain.
2. The following are causes that may lead to confirmed or suspected food safety or suitability

issues:
• Food recall by the supplier or food return by the customer.
• Storing food at an inappropriate temperature.
• Contamination, spoilage, or food exceeding its expiry date.
• No clear label on the food and inability to identify it.
• Evidence of pest infestation.

5.5.17 Food Safety Information Requirements
1. The food establishment must retain the following documents and make them available to
food regulatory authorities, food safety specialists, or any other authorized official. The
specified documents are:
•

Health certificates for food handling employees issued by an accredited body.

2. The following information must be retained and provided:
•

A calorie analysis certificate from an accredited laboratory, or an internal calorie analysis
document prepared within the establishment according to SFDA instructions.

•

Contact numbers for the relevant government authorities in emergencies.

•

Documents may be printed or composed of printed and electronic documents if
establishments use digital solutions.

5.5.18 Reporting Policy Requirements
1. Upon discovering food safety issues, the food establishment must take the following two

actions, without prejudice to the relevant laws and regulations:
• Reporting the issue to the relevant authorities and cooperating in any investigation.
• Ceasing use of the food or ingredient if still under its control, securely isolating it with a

label stating, "unfit for consumption," and storing it optimally as indicated on the product.
Full details of the remaining quantity from the defective batch, if purchased, and the
quantity of materials used must be retained.
2.

The food establishment must report to the relevant authorities if more than two employees
are affected by diarrhea or vomiting while at work.

3. If there are multiple complaints about the same food, its sale must be stopped.
4. When isolating food or ingredients, they must be retained for investigation and testing

purposes.

5.5.19 Traceability and Recall Requirements
1. A traceability system (paper or digital) must be established in the food establishment

covering all food, ingredients, and packaging used in food preparation. This system must
enable the establishment to identify the source and batch details of any ingredient or item,
allowing product recall or supporting non-conformity investigations.
2. The food establishment must retain traceability documents for no less than 180 days after

the expiry of the shelf life, provide them upon request, and be aware of the source of
purchased products and date information for traceability purposes.
3. The supplier name must be recorded in the traceability system upon goods arrival at the

food establishment. The invoice or receipt may be used for this purpose. It may also be
useful to maintain a list of supplier and business customer contact numbers for
emergencies in case of a product recall.

5.6

General Maintenance Requirements:
1.

Periodic and preventive maintenance must be performed on structural elements and all
fittings, utility lines, connections, and equipment, including:
• Maintaining commercial signage and keeping it free from cracks, breakage, and

malfunctions.
• Maintaining the shop/establishment façade and keeping it free from defects such as

breakage, large visible cracks, and visual distortion.
• Maintaining the exterior walls of the shop/establishment and keeping them free from

stickers, defects, and large visible cracks causing visual distortion.
• Maintaining interior floors, walls, and ceilings, keeping them clean and free from

defects and large visible cracks.
• Maintaining air conditioning units, ensuring their effectiveness, the integrity of

connections, and the absence of leaks. Collecting water in open containers is
prohibited..
• Maintaining lighting fixtures periodically, ensuring no malfunctioning or broken bulbs

are present.
• Maintaining service utility lines, including gas, water,sewage, and electrical wiring,

ensuring they are concealed in all interior parts of the shop/establishment, including
ceilings, walls, and floors.
2.

To avoid foreign material contamination risk, the food establishment must ensure food
safety is not affected during maintenance. When immediate maintenance that could risk
contaminating food being produced is needed, food production must stop in the area until
the task is completed and the area is thoroughly cleaned.

5.7

General Cleaning Requirements:
1. Cleaning equipment, detergents, and sanitizers compliant with the approved standard

specifications and intended for use in food handling facilities must be provided.
2. The preparation area must be cleaned and sanitized after handling uncooked food and

before preparing ready-to-eat food.
3. Industrial-grade (not household) cleaning chemicals must always be used, stored in

designated areas, and prepared according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Example:

4. Detergents are used to remove dirt, grease, and residues, while sanitizers reduce

microorganisms to a safe level. Using detergents and sanitizers sequentially is referred to
as a two-stage cleaning process used for deep cleaning. A spray sanitizer may also be
used in a single-stage process for routine cleaning.
• A detergent must be used for the cleaning process, which may involve hot water and soap

or a cleaning product capable of removing dirt, residues, and grease from surfaces and
equipment. Manual scrubbing may be needed to remove some residues. Once equipment
is clean, it should be rinsed with water.
• A sanitizer must be used for the sanitizing process, applied to work surfaces and

equipment and left for the required duration according to the manufacturer's instructions.

5. When deliveries arrive and boxes are placed on food contact surfaces, once all goods are

stored, the food contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized.

6. Dirty kitchen equipment must be cleaned after each use.
7. Sinks must be cleaned after use.
8. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized immediately upon any spills.
9. Work surfaces must be carefully washed between tasks to prevent cross-contamination.
10. Refrigerators must be regularly cleaned and sanitized.
11. All frequently touched areas must be cleaned, such as work surfaces, sinks, faucets, light

switches, refrigerator or freezer handles, can openers, scales, and cash registers.
12. If there is no dishwasher or items cannot be washed in it, the two-stage cleaning process

must be followed:
• Stage One: General cleaning using detergents, including physical removal of visible dirt,

food particles, and residues from surfaces and equipment.
• Stage Two: Sanitizing, including using sanitizers according to the manufacturer's

instructions regarding dilution rate and contact time.

13. When using towels, the food establishment must follow these guidelines:
• Disposable paper towels, discarded after each task.
• Multi-purpose towels cleaned and sanitized after each task and at the end of the day.

14. The same towels cannot be used for floors and other surfaces.
15. If dirty towels contact any kitchen utensils, work surfaces, or equipment, they must be

washed, sanitized, and dried.
16. If dirty towels contact any food, that food must be disposed of.
17. When dedicated sinks are unavailable, time-separation and cleaning controls must be

established. When using the same sink for washing equipment, uncooked food, and
preparing ready-to-eat food, the water must be changed and the sink thoroughly cleaned
and sanitized—including faucets—between uses.
18. Vehicles belonging to the food establishment must be effectively cleaned before use.
19. If equipment is designed for clean-in-place, a combination of chemicals, heat, and water is

used to clean enclosed machines, pipes, or tubing.

20. When cleaning equipment without disassembly:
• The food establishment must ensure detailed cleaning procedures exist and are followed

so that no trace of cleaning chemicals remains in the equipment.
• Chemicals used for cleaning and sanitizing must pass through a fixed system to clean all

internal pipe surfaces.
21. The appearance and cleanliness of furniture such as tables and chairs in the dining area

must be maintained using designated cleaning equipment.

5.7.1 Pest Management Requirements
1. Insect and rodent control devices designed to trap or repel insects must be installed and

positioned so that dead insects or their remains do not fall into exposed food or equipment.
Insect traps must be cleaned regularly or when full.
2. If pest infestation is confirmed, the following actions must be taken by a pest control

contractor:
• Any food contaminated by pests or pest control chemicals must be disposed of. All

affected and surrounding areas, clothing, and equipment must be cleaned and sanitized.
• Rodent and insect pesticides must be used in a manner that does not contaminate food.

They must not be used during food production or preparation, and all exposed food must
be well covered and protected.

3. Any chemicals or tools used in distributing pesticides must be stored safely away from the

kitchen area, in their original containers.
4. Animals—including pets—are prohibited inside or near food handling areas.

5.8

Waste Management Requirements:
1. The requirements and guidelines issued by the Ministry and the National Center for Waste

Management must be followed.
2. Waste inside the food establishment must be:
• Stored in easily accessible containers.
• In standalone units that open by a non-hand-touch mechanism, or placed within the

worktable (without a cover), uncovered during preparation for easy removal for emptying.
• Strong, durable, and capable of being regularly cleaned and sanitized.

3. When food remains in pots, it must be disposed of in a manner that does not pose a

contamination risk.
4. Coffee grounds remaining in the coffee machine head must be disposed of in a separate

drawer (container) before transferring to the waste bin.
5. All food waste must be placed away from the food preparation area in a designated area

before collection. This area must be kept clean, organized, and regularly sanitized to
prevent pest activity.
6. Used and unfit frying fats and oils must be collected in designated sealed containers made

of metal or plastic, labeled with the phrase "fats and oils unfit for human use."
7. Once full, containers must be stored in a separate designated location, away from

containers and packages of usable fats and oils.
8. Used oils and fats must be disposed of according to the relevant laws and instructions.

5.9

Electronic Payment Requirements:
1.

Valid and functional electronic payment methods must be available.

2.

Refusing electronic payment methods is prohibited.

3.

A sticker showing available electronic payment options must be placed on the
shop/establishment facade or inside the building.

5.10

Employee Requirements:
1. The Unified Work Environment Regulation Guide for Private Sector Establishments issued

by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development must be followed regarding
employee break areas, restrooms, employee uniforms, and other requirements, including:
• Workers must wear clean outer clothing that provides a professional appearance

appropriate to their duties.
• Workers must carry work ID cards, or the employee and establishment name must appear

on the establishment uniform.
• All workers must maintain personal hygiene.
• The establishment must not be used for housing.
• Smoking is prohibited except in designated areas.

2. All workers in the food establishment must obtain a health certificate.
3. All food handling workers must be in good health.
4. The food establishment must suspend and dismiss the worker upon the appearance of any

of the following conditions:
• If any symptoms associated with acute infectious intestinal disease appear, such as

diarrhea, fever, or vomiting.
• If diagnosed with a foodborne disease such as cholera, hepatitis, and typhoid/paratyphoid

fever.
• Must not have skin diseases or wounds or sores with discharge on any exposed body part;

must not have any discharge from eyes or nose. Work is permitted if the wound is
superficial, clean, and covered with bandages.
5. Food handling workers with foodborne diseases must not return to work until disease

symptoms have completely disappeared, or after the sick leave issued by the relevant
authority has ended.

6. Food handling workers must wear protective clothing.
7. Workers in food preparation must wear disposable gloves (latex-free) which must be changed

regularly. Gloves are not required for workers operating ovens or high heat sources.
8. Face masks must be worn to cover the nose and mouth in food processing areas.

9. Food handling workers are prohibited from wearing their protective clothing outside the

building or when using restrooms.
10. Gloves must be changed when leaving and returning to the kitchen area, touching any non-

sanitized surfaces such as door handles, or touching any raw food or unwashed fruits and
vegetables.
11. Hands must be washed and gloves changed after handling meat or poultry.
12. Head hair and arms must be securely covered for workers in food preparation.
13. Food handling workers must carefully wash their hands using antibacterial hand soap, dry

them, and change gloves at designated handwashing sinks at the following times:
• Before starting work and after taking a break.
• Before handling food.

• Before handling ready-to-eat food.
• After contact with raw food and its packaging, including unwashed fruits and vegetables.
• After using the restroom.
• After applying or changing a wound bandage.
• After dealing with a sick colleague or customer.
• After contact with pests or their droppings.
• After handling contaminated raw food of animal or plant origin.
• After handling dirty equipment or utensils.
• After sneezing or blowing the nose, coughing, smoking, eating, or drinking.
• After handling animals or waste.
• After performing any activities that may contaminate hands (such as cleaning tasks,

handling money or charcoal, etc.).

14. The following practices that may cause food contamination in food handling areas are

prohibited:
• Smoking, using e-cigarettes, or consuming tobacco.
• Chewing or eating food, sneezing, coughing, or spitting over unprotected food or food

contact surfaces.
• Touching ready-to-eat food without gloves.
• Sitting, lying, or standing on any surface that may come into contact with food.
• Tasting food using fingers.
• Touching hair or other body parts such as the nose, eye, or ear.
• Wearing wristwatches or jewelry.
• Using cosmetics (such as artificial nails, false eyelashes, or nail polish).

Chapter Six

General Provisions and Appeals

6.1 GeneralGeneral
6.2 Appeals and Complaints

General Provisions and Appeals
6.1

General Provisions :
1.

Municipalities and sub-municipalities must monitor the implementation of these
requirements according to their jurisdiction in central kitchens and impose penalties on
violators.

2.

Activity cards on the Baladi platform are an integral part of these requirements, provided
they do not conflict with the requirements set forth herein.

3.

The license holder must comply with the laws and instructions issued by other government
authorities regarding the licensed activity requirements.

4.

Food establishments must comply with the laws, instructions, implementing regulations,
and technical regulations issued by the Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA).

6.2

Appeals against the application of the provisions and regulations set forth in these requirements
may be filed before the appeals and complaints committees at the relevant Municipality / SubMunicipality, in accordance with the Municipal Licensing Procedures Law and its implementing
regulations, and the Municipal Violations Penalties Regulation. With regard to Saudi Building
Code violations, they shall be documented and recorded by the entities responsible for
implementing the Saudi Building Code. Matters outside the Ministry’s jurisdiction may be
appealed before the relevant authorities in accordance with their regulations.
